title: Khadijah hires him
hook: a respected merchant hires him, sees his honesty, and proposes marriage
tomorrow: the black stone on a cloak

segments.voice: Yesterday, amanah, a trust, and a young man the whole town called al-Amin. Your line was be the one they trust.

In Mecca there was a businesswoman. Not a merchant's wife: a merchant. Her name was Khadijah. Widowed, wealthy, respected, from a noble family, she ran her own trading business, hiring men to carry her goods north with the caravans and sell them in Syria. Like any good boss, she paid attention to reputations, and she kept hearing one name. The young man they call al-Amin. Honest. Careful. Doesn't cheat. So she sent for him, and offered him a job.
screen: `A MERCHANT, NOT A MERCHANT'S WIFE.` → `SHE HEARS ONE NAME.` → `SHE OFFERS HIM A JOB.`

segments.voice: Ibn Ishaq's biography says she offered him more than she usually paid, and sent her servant Maysarah along on the journey to Syria. He traded her goods and came home with a profit. But what Maysarah told her about the journey, and about the man, mattered more than the money. So, through a friend, she asked whether he would marry her. Tradition says he was about twenty-five and she about forty; some early reports make her younger. Either way, she was the one who proposed. He accepted, and his uncles arranged the marriage. For as long as she lived, she was his only wife. They had four daughters, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah, and sons who died as little boys. Years after she was gone, he still sent gifts to her old friends, and he's reported in Sahih Muslim to have said simply: I was given her love. The Qur'an describes marriage like this, in Pickthall's words: Allah created mates for you that you might find rest in them, “and He ordained between you love and mercy.” Rest, love, mercy. And here's why today's line matters. Before any angel came to any cave, Khadijah had already seen who he was. She saw him first. Muslim tradition remembers her as the first to accept Islam, and a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari names her among the best of women.
screen: `MAYSARAH REPORTS HIS CHARACTER.` · `SHE PROPOSES.` · `HIS ONLY WIFE WHILE SHE LIVED.` · `I WAS GIVEN HER LOVE.` · then, large: `SHE SAW HIM FIRST.`

segments.voice: Think of someone whose good qualities nobody seems to mention: the coworker who quietly fixes things, the relative who always shows up, the friend who keeps their word. Picture them doing the thing nobody thanks them for, and find the plain words for what you see in them: you're honest, you're steady, you're kind. If you pray, you can ask Allah to reward them.
Khadijah, the merchant who hired him for his honesty, then asked him to marry her, and became his only wife for life.
Your line: she saw him first. Tomorrow, rival clans, one stone, and one cloak. That's day eighty-three.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Khadijah as the Prophet's first wife, the first to accept Islam, and one of the best of women; her marriage is often held up as a model of loyalty and mutual respect.

what a scholar hears: the traditional ages, twenty-five and forty, come from early biographers, and some reports make her younger. and 'Aishah is reported to have said she was never as jealous of anyone as of Khadijah, whom she never met.
